landmarks.name: The Little Mermaid
landmarks.writeup: A famous bronze statue in Copenhagen inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tale.

wiki.extract: The Little Mermaid is a bronze statue by Edvard Eriksen, depicting a mermaid becoming human. The sculpture is displayed on a rock by the waterside at the Langelinie promenade in Copenhagen, Denmark. It is 1.25 metres (4.1 ft) tall and weighs 175 kilograms (385 lb).

landmarks.name: Tivoli Gardens
landmarks.writeup: One of the world's oldest amusement parks located in the heart of Copenhagen.

wiki.extract: Tivoli Gardens, also known simply as Tivoli, is an amusement park and pleasure garden in Copenhagen, Denmark. The park opened on 15 August 1843 and is the second-oldest operating amusement park in the world, after Dyrehavsbakken in nearby Klampenborg, also in Denmark.

landmarks.name: Kronborg Castle
landmarks.writeup: A Renaissance castle in Helsingør, known as the setting of Shakespeare's Hamlet.

wiki.extract: Kronborg is a castle and historical stronghold in the town of Helsingør, Denmark. Immortalised as Elsinore in William Shakespeare's play Hamlet, Kronborg is one of the most important Renaissance castles in Northern Europe. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2000.

landmarks.name: Roskilde Cathedral
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site and burial place of Danish monarchs.

wiki.extract: Roskilde Cathedral, in the city of Roskilde on the island of Zealand (Sjælland) in eastern Denmark, is a cathedral of the Lutheran Church of Denmark.

landmarks.name: Nyhavn
landmarks.writeup: A 17th-century waterfront, canal and entertainment district in Copenhagen.

wiki.extract: Nyhavn is a 17th-century waterfront, canal and entertainment district in Copenhagen, Denmark. Stretching from Kongens Nytorv to the Inner Harbour just south of the Royal Playhouse, it is lined by brightly coloured 17th and early 18th century townhouses and bars, cafes and restaurants. The canal harbours many historical wooden ships.

cultural_events.name: Copenhagen Jazz Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual music festival attracting international jazz artists and audiences.

wiki.extract: Copenhagen Jazz Festival is a jazz event every July in Copenhagen, the capital of Denmark. Copenhagen Jazz Festival was established in 1979, but beginning in 1964 Tivoli Gardens presented a series of concerts under the name Copenhagen Jazz Festival with Thelonious Monk, Miles Davis and many others.

cultural_events.name: Roskilde Festival
cultural_events.writeup: One of Europe's largest music festivals featuring diverse genres.

wiki.extract: The Roskilde Festival is a Danish music festival held annually south of Roskilde. It is one of the largest music festivals in Europe and the largest in the Nordic countries. It was created in 1971 by two high school students and a promoter. In 1972, the festival was taken over by the Roskilde Foundation, which has since run the festival as a non-profit organization for development and support of music, culture and humanism. In 2014, the Roskilde Foundation provided festival participants with the opportunity to nominate and vote upon which organizations should receive funds raised by the festival.

cultural_events.name: Aarhus Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A cultural festival showcasing music, theatre, and art in Denmark's second-largest city.

wiki.extract: Aarhus is the second-largest city in Denmark and the seat of Aarhus Municipality. It is located on the eastern shore of Jutland in the Kattegat sea and approximately 187 kilometres (116 mi) northwest of Copenhagen. Its urban population was 305,227 in 2026.

cultural_events.name: Fastelavn
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional Danish carnival celebrated before Lent with costumes and games.

wiki.extract: Fastelavn is a Carnival tradition in the Northern European, and historically Lutheran, nations of Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Latvia, Estonia, Iceland, Faroe Islands, as well as Greenland.

cultural_events.name: Christmas Markets
cultural_events.writeup: Festive markets held across Denmark featuring crafts, food, and holiday traditions.

wiki.extract: A Christmas market is a street market associated with the celebration of Christmas during the four weeks of Advent. These markets originated in Germany, but are now held in many countries. Some in the U.S. have adapted the German name to quasi-English Christkindlmarket, swapping German Markt and market.

food_writeup: Danish cuisine features open-faced sandwiches called smørrebrød, pastries like Danish wienerbrød, and hearty dishes including pork, potatoes, and rye bread. Seafood is also prominent due to Denmark's coastal geography.
brief_history: Denmark has a history dating back to the Viking Age. It became a unified kingdom in the 10th century and was a major European power in the Middle Ages. Denmark transitioned to a constitutional monarchy in the 19th century and is now a modern welfare state and member of the EU.
current_conflicts: Denmark is not involved in any active military conflicts but participates in international peacekeeping and NATO missions.
